_doc: Build-time TTS manifest, read by tools/tts/render.py. Each entry is one committed WAV. `source.fields` are dotted paths into the named JSON file (a trailing `[]` joins an array field with spaces) — text is resolved AT RENDER TIME from the narrative data, never copy-pasted here, so the spoken line can never drift from the authored text. `register` MUST be "apparatus" — render.py refuses anything else; see its header for the ethics boundary (synthesize the machine, never the person; no TTS on `felt` survivor-side lines).
_docNoBall: ⚑ S79 — THE BALL HAS NO ENTRY HERE, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. data/dialog/s4_ball.json names audio for every MC line and for the room's own bed and landing, and NOT ONE of them may ever be rendered by this pipeline. render.py's own boundary is `register` must be "apparatus" — synthesize the machine, never the person — and TRANSCENDANCE is people: an MC announcing, a room answering, applause. Synthesizing them would make the piece's one respite the only scene in it performed by the apparatus, which is the exact inversion of what the beat is for. ⚑ Those clips wait on real recordings, made with rather than merely about the people this scene is indebted to (ethics #16's reader protocol; docs/research/BALLROOM_PROVENANCE_2026-08-06.md §5). Until they exist, src/audio/tapeAudio.ts's registry law means every name in that file is silently never requested and the captions carry the beat — which is what captions are for. ⚑ If a later session is tempted to add a `ball_*` entry below to hear the timing, do not: render it to a scratch file outside this manifest, and delete it.

entries._doc: S2R.5 (docs/REINTERP_E2_CALEB_SCRIPT_DRAFT_2026-07-24.md) — the PureMail apology, read aloud in LAMBY'S VOICE: the apparatus reading its own death notice in the cheerful assistant timbre. Text is data/dialog/s2_caleb.json's pureMail block (heading + lines + closing), PORTED VERBATIM there from the shipped build per that file's own doc comment — do not rewrite it here or there.

⚑ S77 — L, ERA 4's VOICE. A `batch` entry: render.py walks data/dialog/s4_l.json, finds every object carrying both `text` and `audio`, and renders ALL of them through ONE TTS instance with ONE voice style in ONE process. That is the design constraint, not a convenience — REINTERP_E4_AUDIO_FIRST_DESIGN_2026-07-12.md §4: 'one voice, one description, ALL lines in one batch (drift kills the effect)'. Era 4's premise is a voice that never varies, never tires and never has a bad day; a line rendered in a second sitting would sound like a second machine. Held silences (u3's fourth beat) carry no `audio` key and are skipped, because nothing renders a silence.
entries._docNotRun: ⚑ NOT RUN, AND DELIBERATELY SO. No line of L's is voiced. Clips are generated only AFTER Sérgio's voice pass on the copy (the same order the Lamby entry above followed), because re-rendering thirty lines after a rewrite costs an afternoon and the whole point of one batch is that it happens once. Until then src/audio/tapeAudio.ts's registry law means every filename below is simply never requested — no console error, no 404, captions with no sound. ⚑ AND AFTER the render, somebody must add those filenames to that registry (src/audio/tapeAudio.ts, outside S77's file fence) or the clips still will not play. That is the one wiring step S77 could not take.
entries._docVoice: Voice description for Sérgio's pass, per the design doc §4 and ⚑ corrected by ARGUMENT §4.1 — L MUST SOUND GOOD: 'calm adult voice, ambiguous gender, warm and unhurried, perfectly articulate, studio-clean, no breath sounds, gentle therapeutic cadence, slightly too even.' ⚑ NOT sinister, NOT flat, NOT robotic, and no degradation pass ever: a synthetic voice that reads as a villain lets the real thing off the hook. If a rendered line sounds like a warning, the voice is wrong. `voice`/`speed`/`steps` below are a first guess and are his to change — but change them ONCE, for the whole batch.
